stimulus.description: Demand schedule faced by a single seller (a monopolist) with constant marginal cost and average total cost equal to $20 per unit.

notes: Marginal cost = average total cost = $20 per unit.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: The firm maximizes profit. Calculate the profit-maximizing quantity. Show your work.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets MR = MC (MR = 120 - 2Q) and finds Q = 50 (answer)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the price the firm charges.

rubric_rows.criterion: Reads price from the demand curve at the profit-maximizing quantity (answer)

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the firm's economic profit.

rubric_rows.criterion: Profit = (P - ATC) x Q (answer)

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Calculate the deadweight loss caused by the monopoly relative to the efficient quantity (where P = MC).

rubric_rows.criterion: Computes the triangle with base Q_efficient - Q_monopoly and height P - MC (answer)

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Suppose marginal cost rises by $20 per unit (and demand is unchanged). Does the profit-maximizing quantity increase, decrease, or stay the same? Explain.
parts.model_answer: Quantity decreases: MR = MC now occurs at Q = 40 < 50 because higher marginal cost intersects the same MR curve at a smaller quantity.

rubric_rows.criterion: States quantity decreases and links the higher MC to the MR = MC intersection at a smaller quantity

ap_microeconomics-f02.title: Oligopoly game: dominant strategies and equilibrium

stimulus.description: Payoff matrix for two firms, Airline X (rows) and Airline Y (columns), each choosing to high fare or low fare. Payoffs are profits in millions of dollars, listed as (Airline X, Airline Y).

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Does Airline X have a dominant strategy? If so, identify it.
parts.model_answer: Yes: low fare, since it gives Airline X a higher payoff than high fare regardless of Airline Y's choice.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the dominant strategy and notes it is better regardless of the other firm's choice

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the Nash equilibrium of the game.
parts.model_answer: Both firms choose low fare/low fare: (Airline X: low fare, Airline Y: low fare).

rubric_rows.criterion: States the equilibrium strategy pair

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: What is Airline X's payoff in the Nash equilibrium?
parts.model_answer: $42 million.

rubric_rows.criterion: Reads the equilibrium payoff for the row firm (answer)

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Is there an outcome that gives both firms a higher payoff than the Nash equilibrium? If so, identify it and the payoffs.
parts.model_answer: Yes: (high fare, high fare) gives Airline X $63 million and Airline Y $63 million.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies whether a mutually better outcome exists and states its payoffs (answer)

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Explain why the firms might not reach that outcome without an enforceable agreement.
parts.model_answer: Each firm has an incentive to deviate to its dominant strategy, so the cooperative outcome is not stable without enforcement.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains the incentive to deviate (dominant strategy) makes the cooperative outcome unstable
